h1:
Food Around Thammasat Rangsit
Student Eats, Rice Plates, Milk Tea, Great Value
intro: The Khlong Luang–Rangsit area around Thammasat University is a place where you can eat all day on a budget of a few dozen baht — from single-plate rice dishes and punchy yum salads to sukiyaki and grill buffets, sushi at just over ten baht a piece, and the milk tea students order all semester long. We've picked the spots that are still genuinely open and that locals keep coming back to.

blocks.html: If you're a student at Thammasat University Rangsit Center, or just passing through Khlong Luang, one thing you'll never have to worry about is food. The streets around campus and along Khlong Rangsit are packed with places that price their food for an actual student wallet. You can still find rice-over plates for 50 THB, sushi starting at just over ten baht a piece, sukiyaki and grill buffets under three hundred, and big cups of milk tea that won't dent your allowance. We've sorted everything into categories — from quick single plates to long sit-down meals with friends.
This category is the heart of student life: order it, get it, eat it, and you're back in class. Most plates run 45–60 THB, heavy on the rice and the portion size.

items.name: Baan Jib Restaurant
items.blurb: A made-to-order spot the Thammasat crowd keeps returning to. The menu is homestyle but well cooked — the chicken with cashew nuts and the sour curry with acacia and shrimp are both favorites. Portions are generous and the plate comes piled high, perfect for a day when you just want to eat well without overthinking it.

items.name: Crispy Pork Rice Shop, Thammasat Rangsit
items.blurb: Crispy pork over rice with oyster-sauce gravy for 50 THB a plate — something students order almost daily. The pork is crisp outside and tender inside, and there's also fried rice, stir-fried veggies, egg dishes, and clear soup to switch things up.

items.name: 1000 Nuea (Phan Nuea) — Mingle Market TU
items.blurb: A small step up for the days you're craving beef. The beef curry with braised meat and creamy egg is the standout — tender beef in a rich curry. Located inside Mingle Market on the university side.

blocks.title: Lunch-hour tip
blocks.html: Between 11:30 and 13:00 the rice-over shops around Thammasat get long queues because everyone gets out of class at once. If you can, go before 11:30 or after 1pm — you'll get your food faster and won't have to stand in line.

Yum is the signature food of this area — both build-your-own and house recipes, with that sour–spicy–sweet balance that works over rice or on its own. Prices start in the tens of baht and run up to just over a hundred depending on the ingredients.

items.name: Yum Yupa Thammasat Rangsit
items.blurb: A yum spot the Thammasat crowd knows well. The selling point is that you pick your own ingredients — from moo yor and meatballs to squid and instant noodles. Bold flavors, generous portions, friendly prices.

items.name: Marum Yum, Thammasat Rangsit
items.blurb: The crispy fried squid yum is the most ordered plate — crunchy squid tossed in a sour, spicy dressing. Located in TU Center market, and they deliver if you want it back at the dorm.
items.meta: In TU Center market · from 89 THB

items.name: Yum Yum Cafe, Thammasat University branch
items.blurb: A cafe vibe where you can linger. The yum comes loaded with ingredients, great for a long sit-down with friends. Open until 10pm, so it's an easy evening meet-up spot.

blocks.text: Student-Priced Sushi — Just Over Ten Baht a Piece

blocks.html: Japanese food suits the student budget because you order piece by piece and pay only for what you eat. These two are the spots Rangsit students keep going back to.

items.name: Shinkanzen Sushi
items.blurb: Sushi starting at 11 THB a piece, with thick, fresh-cut salmon. The menu is big and the portions are good for the price — a place the younger crowd around here often mentions as eating their fill for just a couple hundred baht.

items.name: Khai Wan Baan Sushi, Thammasat Rangsit
items.blurb: Sushi at 10–30 THB a piece, with a buy-10-get-1-free deal. It's over by U-Square near the university gate — easy to snack on as you walk back to the dorm without hurting your wallet.

blocks.text: Sukiyaki & Grill Buffets — Long Meals With Friends

blocks.html: Exams done, or the day your parents' allowance lands — buffet is the answer. The Rangsit area has plenty to choose from: sukiyaki, shabu, grill, and mala, all at mid-range prices students can split.

items: Long Mor Suki — all-you-can-eat buffet for 219 THB with a choice of four broths; good for big groups.
Yang Noey, Thammasat Rangsit — grill buffet for 219 THB with good-quality sliced meats. Open 16:00–23:00, made for dinner.
Hohhot Suki — sukiyaki–mala buffet for 269 THB with a rich mala broth and several broths to switch between.
Yakishi Yakiniku — yakiniku-style grill at 309–519 THB with unlimited beef, seafood, and cheese, for the day you want to go all out.

blocks.title: Book ahead for big groups
blocks.html: The buffets around Thammasat fill up on Friday and Saturday evenings. If you're going with a crowd, call ahead to reserve a table so you don't end up waiting in line out front.

blocks.text: Milk Tea & Bubble Tea — Student Prices

blocks.html: Milk tea is the student's go-to drink. Around Thammasat Rangsit there's everything from light-on-the-wallet stalls in the canteen to big-name brands in the mall.

items.name: Ruyi Cha
items.blurb: A bubble milk tea stall inside Thammasat Rangsit's Green Canteen. Easy on the wallet with chewy pearls, and popular simply because it's on campus — an easy walk between classes.

items.name: Kamu Kamu
items.blurb: A milk tea brand students know well — fragrant, with a varied menu from bubble milk tea to other tea drinks. Branches are easy to find around Rangsit.

items.name: Gong Cha — Future Park Rangsit
items.blurb: The well-known bubble tea chain has a spot in Future Park Rangsit, ideal for a day at the mall when you want a familiar milk tea.

blocks.text: Late-Night & Off-Campus Eats in Khlong Luang

blocks.html: Up late studying, or just back from a group project — the Rangsit–Khlong Luang area still has places to grab something to tide you over.

items: Piak Phochana — a well-known late-night rice-porridge spot in the Rangsit–Pathum Thani area, open until around 10pm, with a wide spread of dishes to eat with hot rice porridge.
Jib Dimsum Fusion — fusion dim sum with over 60 items, below Inter Park dorm at Thammasat Rangsit. Open 10:30–21:00 daily, great for snacking in a group.

Krua Baan Jib (Khlong Luang) — a small shop in a soi that locals know, with a good home-cooked touch. Open 10:00–19:00 (closed Saturdays), for a day you want to head off campus and eat somewhere quiet.

blocks.title: On cash and parking
blocks.html: Many student spots in the markets around Thammasat take cash or QR scan only, so keep your banking app ready. As for the shops in the Khlong Luang sois, parking is limited — if you're going in the evening, allow extra time to find a spot.

faq.q: How much do rice-over plates cost around Thammasat Rangsit?
faq.a: Most run 45–60 THB a plate — crispy pork over rice is around 50 THB, and homestyle made-to-order spots like Baan Jib start at 50 THB and up. Beef or more special dishes climb to 80 THB and above.

faq.q: Where should I go for a student-priced buffet around Rangsit?
faq.a: Long Mor Suki and Yang Noey, Thammasat are both 219 THB all-you-can-eat; Hohhot Suki's mala buffet is 269 THB; and for an all-out yakiniku, Yakishi runs 309–519 THB. Pick by your budget and how hungry you are.

faq.q: Which milk tea spots are on the Thammasat Rangsit campus?
faq.a: Ruyi Cha is inside the Green Canteen, easy on the wallet and an easy walk between classes. For bigger brands, Kamu Kamu is easy to find around Rangsit, and Gong Cha has a branch in Future Park Rangsit.

faq.q: Do shops around Thammasat Rangsit take cards or QR payments?
faq.a: Many market and student spots take cash or QR via PromptPay/app transfer mainly. Mall shops like those in Future Park accept cards. Keeping your banking app ready is the easiest way to go.

faq.q: Are there late-night spots around Rangsit–Khlong Luang?
faq.a: Yes. Piak Phochana is a late-night rice-porridge spot in the Rangsit–Pathum Thani area, open until around 10pm, and Yum Yum Cafe's Thammasat branch is also open until 10pm — both good for grabbing food after a late study session.
